question:
Assertion (A): If each element of a row is multiplied by a constant $k$, then the determinant is also multiplied by $k$.

Reason (R): If every entry of a $3 \times 3$ determinant is multiplied by $k$, the value of the determinant is multiplied by $k^3$.
explanation:
Assertion is true: multiplying the elements of a single row by $k$ multiplies the determinant by $k$.

Reason is also true: multiplying all entries of a $3 \times 3$ determinant (i.e., every row and every column by $k$) increases determinant by $k^3$.

But Reason does not explain the Assertion (which pertains to multiplying a single row, not all entries).

So, (B)

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
